correctness.rationale: The separator bijection follows from three disjoint row paths, a two-row bypass when adjacent cut columns differ by two or more, and a discrete intermediate-value barrier when all differences are at most one. The stated initial and terminal move constraints force the sharp lower bound. Parity of coordinate sums and the exact eligibility rule for length-two jumps classify every shortest route; the two outer-jump orders give the closed multiplicities, with boundary cases L=0,1 handled separately. A direct original-graph BFS verified L=0..6, and an independently represented coordinate BFS checked L=0..30. These finite checks corroborate but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimum separators are a natural network-continuity object; migrating a three-vertex barrier from an ingress boundary to an egress boundary without ever opening a path is a motivated optimal-sequence problem. The first width with a central token constrained by two neighbors exhibits a sharp parity-dependent shortest jump-route multiplicity and an asymptotic halving of the slide budget, contrasting the NP-complete general shortest-jump problem. The result is an exact infinite-family optimal-route benchmark, not a table lookup or arbitrary small-sample census.
